title: Wide Table on Facing Pages

illustrates.quote: Wide Tables: Facing Pages. Wide tables may be placed on facing pages in single-sided and interpoint production. Care must be taken to ensure that the first page is on the left-hand page. a. Use the full width of the two pages, usually 80 cells. (See Sample 11-21: Wide Table on Facing Pages on page 11-46.)

print.caption: Unionized Manual Workers
print.notes: Six year-columns (1900-1950) are too wide for a single braille page, so the table is split across two facing braille pages: 1900-1930 on the left page, 1940-1950 on the right page.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box, single header row (years) bold, ruled line beneath; row headings (country names) bold.

pageBreaks.note: No explicit New-Braille-Page marker text. The left-hand braille page (lines 1-12, PDF p. 328/printed 11-46) and the right-hand facing braille page (lines 1-12, PDF p. 329/printed 11-47) are two physically separate, independently-numbered braille pages in the source; detected from the line numbering silently restarting at 1 after the ordinary page footer, with no marker text between them.

braille.notes: Left-hand page: lines 1-2 are the transcriber's note explaining the format (the table is read across facing pages), with a page-number token at the right margin of line 1 per rule 11.13.1.e; the title (Unionized Manual Workers) is centered on this left page only (line 4) per rule g; the box (lines 5-12) shows columns for 1900/1910/1920/1930, with the last column's separation line and guide-dot filler extended to the right margin per rule j/k. Right-hand facing page: begins its own line 1 with a page-number token at the far right and no repeated title (per rule g), its own top/bottom box lines (5, 12), and the first column (1940 data) beginning in cell 1 per rule m, showing only 1940/1950.

uncertain: The precise page-number tokens (right margin of line 1 on each facing page) were transcribed literally; their numeric/lettering meaning (braille page-numbering scheme for facing pages) was not independently decoded.
resolution: print.headers' first cell resolved to '' (blank above the country-name row headings in print, confirmed against the PDF image, p. 328), not a fabricated '(country)' placeholder. pageBreaks schema normalized to run B's object form; both runs already agreed on the facing-pages split itself (after line 12, implicit).
